title: Google Taps Marvell for Custom AI Chips in Deal Worth Up to $12.2 Billion
excerpt: Marvell Technology will develop a range of custom chips for Google's TPU ecosystem, with Google receiving warrants to acquire a stake of up to $12.2 billion tied to purchasing commitments through 2033.
body:
• Marvell Technology will develop custom AI chips for Google, covering accelerators, storage controllers, and networking components for the TPU ecosystem.
  • Google received warrants to purchase up to 58.97 million Marvell shares at $206.58 each — worth roughly $12.18 billion if fully exercised.
  • Warrants vest in quarterly installments through fiscal 2033, tied to Google meeting agreed purchasing targets.
  • Marvell shares surged over 11% premarket while rival Broadcom fell more than 4%, as investors recalibrated the custom-chip landscape.

A New Custom-Chip Partnership Takes Shape

Marvell Technology struck a sweeping agreement with Google to develop custom silicon for the search giant's artificial intelligence infrastructure, the companies disclosed Wednesday in an SEC filing. The deal covers AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute — essentially the full stack of chips that power Google's tensor processing unit ecosystem.

As part of the arrangement, Google received a warrant to buy up to 58.97 million Marvell shares at $206.58 apiece. At that price, a full exercise would be worth approximately $12.18 billion and would make Google Marvell's fifth-largest shareholder, according to LSEG data.

Marvell shares jumped more than 11% in premarket trading on the news. Broadcom, which has served as Google's primary custom-chip partner for years, fell over 4%.

Warrants Tied to Purchasing Commitments

The warrant structure links Google's potential ownership stake directly to how much business it sends Marvell's way. Most of the warrants vest in quarterly installments through fiscal 2033, and will only become available if Google meets agreed purchasing targets over that period.

"The expanded partnership spans a comprehensive range of custom silicon programs."

— Marvell Technology, SEC filing

RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri called the deal "a significant positive" for Marvell, noting that the filing "represents the first official confirmation that Marvell is developing an AI accelerator for Google, validating the company's expanding role in hyperscaler custom silicon." Pajjuri reiterated his outperform rating with a price target of $360.

Reshuffling the Custom-Chip Landscape

The agreement reshuffles competitive dynamics in the custom AI chip market. Broadcom had been Google's primary partner on TPU development and signed a long-term extension in April to supply chips and networking equipment through 2031. Reports earlier this year also indicated Google was working with Taiwan-based MediaTek on future-generation chip designs.

D.A. Davidson managing director Gil Luria said Google appears to be diversifying its chip supply chain as it ramps computing capacity. "Its in-house TPU program has been very successful, and they will create multiple variations of that program," Luria said. He added that Google's stake in Marvell "is a bad sign for Broadcom since it creates a better alignment" between Google and Marvell.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon was more measured, noting that the impact on Broadcom remains unclear. "We do not know how much of the deal is centered on AI vs. more traditional offerings," he said.

Riding the AI Infrastructure Wave

The deal arrives as Big Tech companies have committed to spending more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year, a sharp increase from roughly $400 billion in 2025. Demand for in-house chips like Google's TPUs has surged as companies seek cheaper and more specialized alternatives to Nvidia's graphics processors, particularly for inference — the process of running trained AI models.

Marvell also has custom-silicon engagements with Amazon and Microsoft, according to RBC. Nvidia invested $2 billion in Marvell earlier this year to tighten integration between Marvell's custom chip designs and Nvidia's networking gear.

Marvell, which operates its largest research and development hub outside of California headquarters in India, has steadily repositioned itself from its consumer and storage roots into a hyperscaler custom-silicon partner under CEO Matt Murphy. Wednesday's deal marks the most significant milestone in that transformation.
